title: Steady as the Hills Around Jerusalem
overview: A short pilgrim song that pictures people who trust God as steady as Jerusalem's hills, and hopes that unjust rule over the land will not last.

parts.label: Firm as Mount Zion (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Zion is the hill in Jerusalem where the temple stood, and the city sat among higher hills that sheltered it and made it hard to attack. The psalm compares people who trust God to that unmovable hill and pictures God surrounding them the way those hills surround the city.

parts.label: Unjust rule will not last (v. 3)
parts.note: A scepter was a ruler's staff, so this likely means harsh or foreign rule over the land that was handed out to Israel's families. The worry is that if such rule went on too long, even good people might give up and start doing wrong themselves.

parts.label: A prayer and a warning (vv. 4-5a)
parts.note: The singer asks God to be good to people who are honest at heart, which suggests sincere rather than perfect. Those who drift into crooked ways are pictured being led off with the wrongdoers, possibly like prisoners being marched away.

parts.label: A closing blessing (v. 5b)
parts.note: The psalm ends with a brief blessing of peace spoken over the whole people of Israel. It can be read either as a wish or as a promise.

think: When you have felt most steady in your life, what was it that held you in place?
